notes.meaning: The psalmist asks why God feels so far away during painful moments. When hard times hit, the Lord can seem to hide His face or stand back like a quiet spectator. God's people are not wrong to feel this sorrow, and this honest question brings their hurt directly to Him in prayer.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: In the ancient Greek and Latin translations used in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, Psalms 9 and 10 are joined together as one single psalm.

notes.meaning: A proud, wicked person uses his power to hunt down and abuse the poor. The psalmist asks God to turn those very traps back onto the schemers who made them. It is right and just for bullies to get caught in their own cruel plots.

The wicked man openly brags about his greedy cravings and sinful success. Instead of honoring God, he praises other selfish people and despises the Lord. He values money and selfish desire far more than God's approval.

Deep pride keeps the wicked man from seeking God or asking Him for help. He is too stubborn to bend his knee, and his daily plans leave no room for God at all. He lives in practice as if the Lord does not exist or has no say over his life.

The wicked man seems to succeed in all his ways, which makes him reckless and overconfident. Because God does not punish him right away, he treats God's laws as distant rules that do not matter to him. He sneers at his enemies, wrongly believing no one can ever bring him down.

In his heart, the wicked man boasts that nothing can ever shake his comfort or bring him ruin. His continuous success tricks him into thinking his good fortune will last forever. Such false security blinds him to the fact that all human pride will come to an end.

The mouth of the wicked is filled with curses, lies, and threats. Beneath his words hide harmful schemes ready to cause misery and trouble for others. What comes out of his mouth simply shows the deep malice living in his heart.

The oppressor acts like a bandit hiding near village roads to ambush innocent travelers. He watches quietly for helpless victims who cannot defend themselves. He hides his actions not out of shame, but so his violent traps will work without warning.

He is compared to a hungry lion crouching in the thick brush, waiting to leap on its prey. He also acts like a hunter spreading a net to drag away the poor. These word pictures show just how cruel and calculating his attacks on godly people are.

The predator crouches down low to hide his strength until the moment is right. Then he strikes, and the helpless victim is crushed beneath his power. Even when such wicked people act quiet or humble, their only goal is to ruin the weak.

The wicked man reassures himself by claiming God has forgotten and will never notice what he does. Because the Lord does not strike immediately, the sinner foolishly thinks heaven is blind to his crimes. He misreads God's patience as permission to keep doing evil.

The psalmist calls on the Lord to rise up and show His mighty power. He pleads with God not to forget the humble, hurting people who are being mistreated. Real faith boldly asks God to step into human history when all earthly help fails.

The psalmist asks why evil men are allowed to despise God and boast that they will never be judged. The sinner tells himself that God will never call him to give an account for what he has done. Yet God's delay is simply His patience giving room before the day of judgment arrives.

God truly sees all the pain, grief, and mischief that bullies cause, and He takes note of it to repay them with His own hand. Helpless people, like orphans who have no human protector, can safely entrust their lives to Him. The Lord has always been a faithful father and helper to the defenseless.

The prayer asks God to break the arm of the wicked, which means taking away their power to harm others. It calls on the Lord to search out all their evil deeds until every wrong is judged and stopped. When God removes a tyrant's strength, the oppressed are finally set free.

The Lord rules as the eternal King forever, outlasting every earthly empire and ruler. Just as He cleared wicked nations out of the Promised Land in past times, He will clear all oppressors from the earth. Believers can take comfort knowing God's royal throne will never fall.

The Lord hears even the quiet desires and unexpressed sighs of humble hearts. He first prepares their hearts to pray and gives them strength, and then He leans down to listen. God never turns away the sincere cries of those who lean on Him.

God will defend the fatherless and crushed victims, giving them full justice. When He steps forward, mortal bullies made of earthly dust will no longer be able to terrorize anyone. Human oppressors are weak and temporary compared to the living God of heaven.
